title: The LLM bill is too high
brief: A 'summarize this product page' feature runs on 16 GPU replicas: $48/hr for 40 requests/s. Finance wants the bill cut by more than half, without making users wait longer. Find where the money goes, then cut it.

requirements: 70% are for the same popular products: an answer cache can hit at most 0.7
variants.twist: Product pages change hourly, so the cache TTL drops and the hit ratio falls to 0.4 (set hit_ratio 0.4). What does that cost?

requirements: 40 requests/s, all unique: no cache helps
Summaries can arrive a few minutes later by notification: the request only has to be accepted
A replica fed from a queue can batch: about 10 summaries/s at about 4 s each (set capacity_rps 10, base_latency_ms 4000). Only worth it if nobody waits
variants.twist: Launch day doubles requests for a while: spike(multiplier=2, seconds=30). Let the backlog grow, or add GPUs? What's the cost of each?

hints: How busy is each GPU right now? How many of these requests needed a GPU at all?
16 replicas take 80/s and you send 40: first right-size the pool. Then: repeated prompts can come from a cache, and if nobody waits, bigger batches trade latency for throughput.
Repeats: cache (hit 0.7) in front of the LLM, 3 replicas. Batch: service -> queue -> worker -> LLM set to capacity_rps 10 and base_latency_ms 4000, 5 replicas; the service only enqueues.
_notes: Starter: client (timeout 60 s) -> LB -> 2 services (timeout 60 s) -> LLM x16: rho 0.5, p99 ~2.5 s, $48.23. Just right-sizing to 9 replicas (rho 0.89) gives $27.23: half the bill, still over both budgets. Repeats: cache 0.7 -> LLM sees 12/s. 3 replicas: p99 ~2.6 s, $9.38; 4 ($12.38) break the budget. Batch: queue -> 1 worker -> LLM (10/s, 4 s). 5 replicas (rho 0.8): accept p99 ~37 ms, $15.38; 3 fall behind; 6 ($18.38) break the budget. The same batched replicas behind a waiting user give p99 ~5 s. Also worth raising: a smaller model, shorter prompts, prompt caching. Cost per token isn't modeled; the sim prices GPU-hours. Checked in frontend/src/lessons/content.test.ts.
